After one year of [[college basketball]] with the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]], he was drafted third overall by the 76ers in the [[2014 NBA draft]]. The {{convert|7|ft|m|2|adj=on}} center is a seven-time [[NBA All-Star]], a five-time member of the [[All-NBA Team]], a three-time member of the [[NBA All-Defensive Team|All-Defensive Team]], and a two-time [[List of NBA annual scoring leaders|NBA scoring champion]]. He was named the [[NBA Most Valuable Player]] (MVP) in 2023. Embiid also won a gold medal on the [[2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2024 U.S. Olympic team]].{{cite web |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/paris-2024/athlete/joel-embiid_1954683 |title=EMBIID Joel |work=[[Paris 2024 Olympics]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240730143617/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/athlete/joel-embiid_1954683 |archive-date=30 July 2024}} Multiple foot and knee injuries delayed Embiid's debut for two seasons until 2016–17 when he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]] despite playing only 31 games. |url=http://grantland.com/features/joel-embiid-nba-draft-philadelphia-76ers-kansas-jayhawks/ |access-date=27 June 2014 |publisher=Grantland |date=27 June 2014 |archive-date=29 June 2014 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070988 |title=Embiid's double-double powers 76ers past Knicks 117–91 |publisher=ESPN |date=28 November 2018 |access-date=28 November 2018 |quote=Thomas |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181129100427/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070988 |url-status=live}} He played [[volleyball]] and [[soccer]]{{cite web |last=Campitelli |access-date=23 September 2020 |website=nbcsportsphiladelphia.com}} in childhood and originally planned to play professional volleyball in Europe but started playing basketball at age 15, modeling his game after NBA [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Fame]] center [[Hakeem Olajuwon]].{{cite news |last=DeCourcy |first=Mike |title=Joel Embiid's pursuit of hoops greatness not just a Dream |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2014-01-22/joel-embiid-kansas-jayhawks-nba-draft-no-1-pick-center-hakeem-olajuwon-cameroon |access-date=27 June 2014 |publisher=The |url-status=dead}} Embiid was discovered at a basketball camp by [[Luc Mbah a Moute]], a fellow native of Yaoundé and an NBA player.{{cite web |last=Dodd |first=Rustin |date=16 May 2014 |title=Report: Kansas basketball star Joel Embiid will enter NBA Draft |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article343459/Report-Kansas-basketball-star-Joel-Embiid-will-enter-NBA-Draft.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180811032346/https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article343459/Report-Kansas-basketball-star-Joel-Embiid-will-enter-NBA-Draft.html |archive-date=11 August 2018 |access-date=22 October 2016 |work=The Kansas City Star}} With Mbah a Moute as his mentor, Embiid moved to the United States at age 16 to devote himself to becoming a professional basketball player.{{cite news |last=Telep |first=Dave |date=13 November 2012 |title=Kansas lands recruit Joel Embiid |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/8627432 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006181910/http://espn.go.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/8627432/joel-embiid-makes-verbal-commitment-kansas-jayhawks |archive-date=6 October 2014 |access-date=27 June 2014 |publisher=ESPN}} Embiid enrolled at [[Montverde Academy]], Mbah a Moute's alma mater, but transferred after his first year due to a lack of playing time.{{cite magazine |last=Jenkins |first=Lee |title=Joel Embiid: 'I'm The Process' |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2016/10/26/joel-embiid-philadelphia-76ers-the-process/ |access-date=27 October academy, in [[Gainesville, Florida]]. As a senior, he led their team to a 33–4 record and state championship, averaging 13.0 points, 9.7 rebounds and 1.9 blocks per game. Embiid was a [[college recruiting#Star ratings|five-star recruit]] according to [[Rivals.com]]{{cite web |title=KU's Embiid grows as a basketball player |url=http://www.kansascity.com/2013/12/09/4682046/kus-embiid-grows-as-a-basketball.html |access-date=18 March 2014 |archive-date=18 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140318104514/http://www.kansascity.com/2013/12/09/4682046/kus-embiid-grows-as-a-basketball.html |url-status=dead}}{{cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Joel-Embiid-143044 |title=Joel Embiid |publisher=Yahoo! Sports |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150712005749/https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Joel-Embiid-143044 |archive-date=12 July 2015}} and committed to [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] in November 2012. ==College career== [[File:Joel Embiid 2014.jpg|thumb|upright|right|Embiid with the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] in 2014]] Embiid attended the [[University of Kansas]] for one year alongside notable teammate [[Andrew Wiggins]]. On 13 February 2014, he was named one of the 30 finalists for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].{{cite web |title=2013–14 Men's Naismith Trophy Midseason 30 |url=http://www.naismithawards.com/PressBox/ArticleView/tabid/209/ArticleId/8/2013-14-Mens-Naismith-Trophy-Midseason-30.aspx |work=Naismith Awards |access-date=14 February 2014 |date=13 February 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222224557/http://www.naismithawards.com/PressBox/ArticleView/tabid/209/ArticleId/8/2013-14-Mens-Naismith-Trophy-Midseason-30.aspx |archive-date=22 February 2014}} In 2013–14, he played 28 games, averaging 11.2 points, 8.1 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 2.6 blocks in 23.1 minutes per game.{{cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/joel-embiid-1.html |title=Joel Embiid Stats |work=Sports-reference |access-date=2 October 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006070621/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/joel-embiid-1.html |archive-date=6 October 2014}} He had over 15 points in seven games and over 5 blocks in six games. He subsequently earned [[Big 12]] Defensive Player of the Year honors and was named second-team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big 12]]. Embiid suffered a stress fracture in his back in March 2014.{{cite web |last=Goodman |first=Jeff |date=11 March 2014 |title=Joel Embiid out indefinitely |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10585990 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006124752/http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10585990/joel-embiid-kansas-jayhawks-indefinitely-getting-second-opinion |archive-date=6 October 2014 |access-date=1 October 2014 |publisher=ESPN}} He missed that year's [[2014 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]] and [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. Kansas lost in the second round (round of 32) of the NCAA tournament. ==Professional career== ===2014 NBA draft=== On 9 April 2014, Embiid declared for the [[2014 NBA draft]], forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.{{cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/nba/point-forward/2014/04/09/joel-embiid-declares-draft-kansas |title=Kansas' Joel Embiid declares for 2014 NBA draft |magazine=Sports Illustrated |last=Golliver |first=Ben |date=9 April 2014 |access-date=1 October 2014 |archive-date=6 October 2014 broken navicular bone in his right foot, and was subsequently ruled out for four to six months.{{cite web |url=http://www.foxsports.com/ohio/story/nba-draft-how-far-will-embiid-fall-062114 |title=No. overall pick by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web |date=27 June 2014 |others=Contributed by Royce Young and The Associated Press |title=Sixers draft Joel Embiid at No. 3 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2014/story/_/id/11141687 |url-status=live 2014 |access-date=1 October 2014 |publisher=ESPN}} That selection made him the third Cameroonian-born NBA player after [[Ruben Boumtje-Boumtje]] and [[Luc Mbah a Moute]], as well as the highest 2014]] On 26 August 2014, Embiid signed his rookie scale contract with the 76ers.{{cite web |url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234735/Joel-Embiid-Signs-Rookie-Deal-With-76ers |title=Joel Embiid |url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234734/76ers-Unsure-If-Joel-Embiid-Will-Play-At-All-This-Season |title=76ers Unsure If Joel Embiid Will Play At All This Season |publisher=RealGM Wiretap |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/statement-sixers-gm-sam-hinkie |title=Statement from Sixers GM Sam Hinkie |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=13 June 2015 |access-date=14 June 2015 in Game 6, advance to East semifinals |url=https://www.nba.com/game/phi-vs-tor-0042100136 |website=NBA.com |access-date=29 April 2022 |date=29 April 2022 |archive-date=7 May 2022 He became the first player in NBA history with 50 points, 10 boards, five assists and five blocks in a game since blocks became an official stat in the [[1973–74 NBA season|1973–74 season]]. This was also the fifth-best scoring performance in 76ers franchise history. He managed to top 101 total points in less than 24 hours, following up a 42-point, 10-rebound and six-assist performance on 12 November in a 121–109 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite web |title=Embiid scores career-high 59, leads 76ers past Jazz 105–98 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/401468350 |access-date=14 November 2022 |website=ESPN |language=en |archive-date=13 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221113205510/https://www.espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/401468350 |url-status=live}}{{Cite web |title=Joel Embiid demolishes the box score, delivers unprecedented performance |url=https://www.nba.com/news/joel-embiid-career-high-59-point-performance |access-date=14 November 2022 |website=NBA.com |archive-date=14 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221114034944/https://www.nba.com/news/joel-embiid-career-high-59-point-performance |url-status=live}} On 11 December, Embiid had 53 points and 11 rebounds, leading the Philadelphia 76ers to a 131–113 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. He became the third player in 76ers franchise history to have multiple 50-point games in the same season, joining [[Allen Iverson]] (2000–01 and 2004–05) and [[Wilt Chamberlain]] (1965–66 and 1967–68). It is also the 30th game in Embiid's career with 40 points and 10 rebounds. The only other player in franchise history to accomplish that feat was Chamberlain.{{Cite web |title=Embiid scores 53, leads 76ers to 131–113 win over Hornets |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468554 |access-date=12 December 2022 |website=ESPN.com |archive-date=12 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221212022100/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468554 |url-status=live}} On 23 December, Embiid put up 44 points and seven rebounds in a 119–114 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. He also surpassed Wilt Chamberlain for the second-most 40-point games in 76ers franchise history.{{cite web |url=https://clutchpoints.com/sixers-news-joel-embiid-passes-wilt-chamberlain-in-philly-history-leaving-only-allen-iverson-to-chase |title=Joel Embiid passes Wilt Chamberlain in Sixers history leaving only Allen Iverson to chase |website=ClutchPoints |last=Guinhawa |first=Angelo |date=27 December 2022 |access-date=27 December 2022 |archive-date=28 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221228035351/https://clutchpoints.com/sixers-news-joel-embiid-passes-wilt-chamberlain-in-philly-history-leaving-only-allen-iverson-to-chase |url-status=live}} On 3 January, Embiid was awarded the Eastern Conference [[2022–23 NBA season|Player of the Month]] award for his play during the month of December, the fifth of his career, breaking a tie with Allen Iverson for the most such honors in 76ers franchise history.{{Cite web |title=Luka Doncic, Joel Embiid named Kia Players of the Month |url=https://www.nba.com/news/kia-players-of-the-month-dec-2022-23 |access-date=3 January 2023 |website=NBA.com |language=en |archive-date=3 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230103214802/https://www.nba.com/news/kia-players-of-the-month-dec-2022-23 |url-status=live}} [[File:20230416 8thMONTROSE MVP.jpg|thumb|left|Joe Boruchow's Embiid MVP poster on S 9th St by Montrose in Philadelphia's Italian Market in April 2023]] On 28 January, Embiid recorded 47 points, a season-high 18 rebounds, 5 assists, 3 steals and 2 blocks in a 126–119 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]]. He became the second player in 76ers franchise history to produce at least four games of 45-plus points, 15-plus rebounds and five-plus assists, joining Wilt Chamberlain. Embiid also became just the third player in NBA history to record at least 47 points, 18 rebounds, five assists, three steals and two blocked shots. He joined Hall of Famers [[Chris Webber]] (5 January 2001) and [[Bob McAdoo]] (18 March 1975) with such games.{{Cite web |title=Joel Embiid Drops 47 in Showdown with Jokic, Nuggets; Sixers Win Seventh Straight |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/joel-embiid-scores-47-vs-nikola-jokic-nuggets |access-date=4 February 2023 |website=NBA.com |language=en |archive-date=4 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230204004941/https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/joel-embiid-scores-47-vs-nikola-jokic-nuggets |url-status=live}} For his play in January, Embiid took home the Eastern Conference Player of the Month, the sixth of his career and second in a row. He also put up his ninth consecutive 30-point game, surpassing Allen Iverson and Wilt Chamberlain for the most consecutive games with at least 30 points in 76ers franchise history.{{cite web |url=https://clutchpoints.com/sixers-news-joel-embiid-passes-allen-iverson-wilt-chamberlain-for-solo-76ers-record |title=Joel Embiid passes Allen Iverson, Wilt Chamberlain for solo Sixers record |website=ClutchPoints |last=Villas |first=Rexwell |date=18 March 2023 |access-date=18 March 2023 |archive-date=19 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319030939/https://clutchpoints.com/sixers-news-joel-embiid-passes-allen-iverson-wilt-chamberlain-for-solo-76ers-record |url-status=live}} On 4 April, Embiid scored 52 points on 20-of-25 shooting from the field, along with 13 rebounds, six assists and two blocks in a 103–101 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web |url=https://clutchpoints.com/sixers-news-joel-embiids-monster-night-vs-celtics-leaves-luka-doncic-with-another-backbreaking-challenge |title=Joel Embiid's monster night vs Celtics leaves Luka Doncic with another backbreaking challenge |website=ClutchPoints |last=Villas |first=Rexwell |date=4 April 2023 |access-date=4 April 2023 |archive-date=5 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230405054805/https://clutchpoints.com/sixers-news-joel-embiids-monster-night-vs-celtics-leaves-luka-doncic-with-another-backbreaking-challenge |url-status=live}} He became just the second player in NBA history to produce a stat line of at least 50–10–5 while shooting 80% or better. Embiid also joined Wilt Chamberlain and [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]] as the only three centers to have three 50-plus-point games in a season in NBA history.{{Cite web |title=Kia MVP Ladder: Joel Embiid reclaims top spot, but nothing is 'over' yet |url=https://www.nba.com/news/kia-mvp-ladder-april-7-2023-edition |date=7 April 2023 |access-date=8 April 2023 |website=NBA.com |language=en |archive-date=8 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230408030507/https://www.nba.com/news/kia-mvp-ladder-april-7-2023-edition |url-status=live}} On 9 April, Embiid was named the NBA scoring champion, averaging 33.1 points per game, doing so for the second straight season.
